[color=#ffff00][head=3]Escalation Guidelines[/head][/color]
[color=#FFFACD]Playing as an antagonist is allowed, to grant players freedom in the characters they play. This does not mean that you should be picking fights constantly. Murder and killing should be a last resort. An antagonist exists to generate and enhance stories, not to detract from them.[/color]
[color=#FFFACD]When generating conflict or performing disruptive activities, be mindful of the escalation rules below and whether your character has reasonable justification to escalate.[/color]
[color=#a4885c]IE.1[/color] Ships that are marked as ØPacifistØ are not to initiate or to be included in any form of PvP content, including any crew aboard the ship. [color=#cc0000]★★★[/color]
[color=#a4885c]IE.2[/color] Escalate conflicts reasonably. Use common sense when deciding how far a situation should go. A spilled drink might lead to an argument or fistfight, but should not escalate into a gunfight. [color=#f1c232]★★[/color]
[color=#a4885c]IE.3[/color] When instigating follow these steps and allow time for the other party to react to each step as you go through them: [color=#f1c232]★★[/color]
[color=#a4885c]i.[/color] Initiate with talking, establishing what will happen.
[color=#a4885c]ii.[/color] Threaten with violence.
[color=#a4885c]iii.[/color] Fire a warning shot if possible.
- [color=#a4885c]IE.3A[/color] Defenders of aggression can escalate freely for the purposes of protecting themselves, this includes if someone has entered your ship.
- [color=#a4885c]IE.3B[/color] If you attempt to coerce someone through threats of escalation, and they refuse, you can treat that as consent to escalate further. Threats of escalation must not be excessive in nature.
[color=#a4885c]IE.4[/color] When players are engaging in roleplay such as hostage-taking, robberies, or otherwise, do not transition to mechanical combat while they are still roleplaying or typing. Players are expected to engage in good faith, even if this puts them at a disadvantage. ★
[color=#a4885c]IE.5[/color] If someone is surrendering, you must accept it, no matter how heated a situation is. Surrendering is an 'opt-out' for PvP interactions, please talk in LOOC after a surrender, to determine what would be a preferred outcome to the scene. Under no circumstances are you to falsely surrender. [color=#f1c232]★★[/color]
[color=#a4885c]IE.6[/color] Do not intentionally round-remove characters. If you kill someone, you are not expected to revive them, but you must not take any actions that will round-remove them. [color=#f1c232]★★[/color]
- [color=#a4885c]IE.6A[/color] Emotional Support Pets, and Borgs also apply to this role when selected as Ghost Roles. Other Ghost Roles such as antagonistic ghost roles or vermin animals (mice, mothroaches) are exempt and can be round-removed.
- [color=#a4885c]IE.7[/color] Do not use ERP, the offer of ERP, Privacy Holobarriers or the ØPacifistØ or ◄PRIVATE► ship IFF markers, as a means of forwarding any antagonistic goals. ★
[color=#a4885c]IE.8[/color] Ship to Ship combat follows the standard escalation rules, with additional clarifications made below. [color=#f1c232]★★[/color]
- [color=#a4885c]IE.8A[/color] When an opposing ship has stopped moving or firing its guns at you, cease fire, then if there are no further targets request that they surrender.
- [color=#a4885c]IE.8B[/color] Do not fire upon a ship that has lost combat capabilities, but is still operational. For example, its pilot has been killed.
- [color=#a4885c]IE.8C[/color] When demanded to surrender, you do not need to surrender, but you must respond if capable, shooting qualifies as a response. No response is considered a surrender.
